q7.answer: Not decided. The brief does not say how a flag change reaches workers, and I never chose a mechanism. The document only says workers read the flag from the config service and keep their last known mode if it is unreachable. A stale worker is stopped from double charging by the customer and period charge key check. What a worker does with an invoice it started under the old value is also undecided, and both are listed as open questions.

q8.answer: Gate evidence is the nightly comparison results kept per day (streak, invoice count, unresolved mismatch list). Promotion goes through the rollout controller, which refuses an advance command unless the gate is met. Meeting a gate never moves the mode by itself. Finance sign-off is also checked for both to new_only. Who may send the advance command is not decided.

q9.answer: The rollout controller detects it. It measures the new engine's charge failure rate over a sliding 10-minute window, in both or new_only only. Above 2% it starts the rollback itself at Hold. What counts as a failure and any minimum charge volume are not decided and are listed as open questions.

q10.answer: During Hold, normal charge requests wait and are retried after the hold ends. They are not dropped. Due charges found in Reconcile (ledger invoices with no charge for that customer and period key) are made by the old engine in Resume step (b). These are exempt from the hold and use the ledger invoice amount. Normal charging resumes when the hold is cleared at the end of Resume.

q11.answer: The customer and period charge key. Reconcile looks up every period with a ledger invoice in the ledger and at the payment provider, so a charge the new engine already made, or one with an unknown outcome, shows as charged and is skipped. Resume charges only periods with no charge for that key. The new engine is stopped first. This key check is my design requirement, not something in the brief.

q12.answer: The rollback goes to Blocked and on-call is paged. The hold stays on, the flag is unchanged, and the new engine stays stopped if Resume had already stopped it, because the controller records that. Some due charges may already be made. On-call retries and the run restarts from Reconcile. Reconcile rebuilds the due list from the ledger and provider and skips periods already charged by key. Reprocess rewrites the same keyed invoices, so a rerun is safe.
